item.title: Emerald Beach — Guide
item.description: Emerald Beach is a lovely, immaculately maintained public beach within Ocean Expo Park on the Motobu Peninsula in northern Okinawa, right beside the famous Churaumi Aquarium. True to its name, it fronts clear emerald and turquoise water, with soft white sand divided into distinct areas for swimming, playing and relaxing. Because it’s a park beach, it’s exceptionally clean, safe and well-equipped, with lifeguards during the season, showers, rest areas and a calm, netted swimming zone — making it ideal for families and less confident swimmers.

item.title: Itoshima Peninsula and Futamigaura Beach — Guide
item.description: The Itoshima Peninsula, a short drive west of Fukuoka city, has become one of the region’s most popular getaways — a relaxed stretch of coastline mixing beaches, surf, farm produce and a thriving scene of stylish seaside cafes, bakeries and craft studios. Its most photogenic sight is Futamigaura, where a pair of sacred ‘married rocks’ (meoto-iwa) linked by a sacred rope stand in the sea beside a striking white torii gate, framing spectacular sunsets over the water.

item.title: Katsurahama Beach and the Ryoma Statue — Guide
item.description: Katsurahama is one of Kochi’s most beloved beaches, a scenic crescent of sand backed by green pines and framed by rocky headlands where the Pacific rolls in. Long celebrated as a spot for moon-viewing, it is more a place for scenery than swimming — the waves and currents can be strong — and its great landmark is the towering bronze statue of Sakamoto Ryoma, the Kochi-born samurai visionary who helped bring about the Meiji Restoration and the birth of modern Japan.

item.title: Kouri Island & Bridge — Guide
item.description: Kouri Island (Kourijima), a small round island off the Motobu Peninsula in northern Okinawa, is one of the island’s most beloved scenic spots, famous above all for the spectacular drive across the Kouri Bridge that connects it to the mainland. Nearly 2 km long and flanked by dazzling turquoise and emerald sea, the bridge is a highlight in itself, and the view from either end is unforgettable. On the island, Kouri Beach beside the bridge offers clear, shallow water perfect for swimming and photos, while on the north coast the famous ‘Heart Rock’ — two rock formations that together frame a heart shape — is a hugely popular photo spot, especially with couples.

item.title: Seagaia Resort — Guide
item.description: Seagaia is a large integrated seaside resort on the Pacific coast just north of Miyazaki city, set within a beautiful expanse of coastal pine forest known as Hitotsuba. Making the most of Miyazaki’s warm, sunny, resort-like climate, the complex brings together a range of leisure and relaxation facilities in one place: luxury and family hotels including a landmark tower hotel, championship golf courses, a tennis centre, a soothing hot-spring spa (Matsu no Yu), restaurants and event spaces, all a short distance from the beach.

item.title: Surfing in Miyazaki — Guide
item.description: Miyazaki is one of Japan’s premier surfing destinations, blessed with a warm subtropical climate, consistent year-round swells rolling in off the Pacific, and long stretches of sandy beach. The most famous spot is Kisakihama, a long beach south of Miyazaki city that regularly hosts national and international surfing competitions, with reliable, well-shaped waves that draw serious surfers from across Japan. But Miyazaki’s coast also has plenty of gentler beach breaks perfect for beginners, and a lively local surf culture with surf schools, board rental and laid-back beachside cafés.

item.title: Yonaha Maehama Beach — Guide
item.description: Yonaha Maehama Beach, on the southwest coast of Miyako Island, is frequently ranked among the most beautiful beaches in Japan — and is sometimes called ‘the finest beach in the Orient’. Stretching for around 7 km, it’s a breathtaking ribbon of fine, powder-white sand meeting exceptionally clear, shimmering turquoise water, with gentle shallows that make it superb for swimming. Facing west across the sea toward Kurima Island (linked by a bridge), it’s also one of Okinawa’s premier sunset spots, with glorious evening skies over the water.

item.title: Kujukuri Beach Guide: Japan's Longest Beach & Access
item.description: Stretching some 60 kilometres in a near-straight line down Chiba’s Pacific coast, Kujukuri Beach is one of the longest beaches in Japan — an immense ribbon of sand, surf and big sky. Its name (“99 ri”) nods to its legendary length, and its open eastern aspect makes it a famous spot to watch the sunrise over the ocean. Long a centre of the iwashi (sardine) fishing industry, today it’s a summer playground for swimming, surfing, beachcombing and seaside seafood, with a refreshingly wild, uncommercialised feel.

item.title: Onjuku & Southern Boso Coast Guide: Beaches & Access
item.description: The breezy resort town of Onjuku, on Chiba’s outer Boso coast, is a classic Japanese seaside escape — a crescent of white sand and turquoise shallows that has drawn beachgoers since the early 20th century. Gentle, clean and family-friendly, Onjuku Beach is great for swimming and lazing, watched over by a quirky “Tsukimi” mermaid statue and a monument commemorating the 1609 rescue of shipwrecked Spanish sailors bound for Mexico (the town’s enduring link to Acapulco).

item.title: Wakayama Family Trip: Pandas, Beach Fun & Kid-Friendly Temples
item.description: Wakayama works well for families in a way that some of Japan’s more densely cultural prefectures do not: there are genuine natural spectacles that children find compelling without requiring adult interpretive scaffolding, a world-class animal park that delivers on its panda promise, beaches that are genuinely safe for small children, and a spiritual mountain that manages to be simultaneously solemn and otherworldly enough to captivate curious kids. The distances between main attractions require planning — this is not a prefecture you can improvise with young children — but a well-structured 3–4 day itinerary produces one of the most varied family travel experiences in western Japan.

item.title: Chiba Family Trip: Disney, Beaches, Wildlife & Kids' Attractions
item.description: Chiba is one of the best prefectures in Japan for a family trip. It holds the country’s most visited theme park complex, a world-class aquarium, Japan’s longest beach, and a whole peninsula of coastal scenery and wildlife encounters within easy reach of Tokyo. Children aged 3 to 15 will find something genuinely exciting at almost every stop, and the prefecture’s flat terrain and excellent rail connections make logistics manageable. Tokyo Disney Resort — The Family Centrepiece For most families visiting Chiba, Tokyo Disney Resort is the main reason they came.

item.title: Chiba Nature Guide: Kujukuri Beach, Boso Peninsula & Coastal Landscapes
item.description: Chiba Prefecture is the closest coastal wilderness to Tokyo — a long peninsula curling into the Pacific with 66 kilometres of unbroken sandy beach on one side, dramatic cliffs and fishing villages on the other, and a forested interior largely unknown to foreign visitors. Its natural landscapes shift with the seasons in ways that reward return visits: winter flower fields, spring rapeseed and cherry blossoms along a country railway line, summer surf beaches, and autumn foliage in the gorge country of the central hills.

item.title: Okinawa Family Trip Guide: Beaches, Aquarium, Theme Parks & Kids' Activities
item.description: Okinawa is Japan’s best family travel destination — the combination of warm, calm, shallow seas (safe for young children), world-class marine attractions, year-round outdoor activities, and family-friendly resort facilities creates a trip that works for everyone from toddlers to teenagers. Japan’s highest concentration of family beach resort hotels is right here. Why Okinawa Is Perfect for Families Warm, calm water year-round — the East China Sea is sheltered and shallow at most beach resorts; perfect for small children No cold season — even January averages 18–20°C; outdoor activities work every month Marine life is exceptional — sea turtles, whale sharks, tropical fish, and coral reefs accessible without scuba Resort facilities — kids' pools, shallow lagoon pools, beach water sports rentals, and children’s menus at all major resorts Safe and easy to navigate — Japan’s safety standards are world-leading; beaches have lifeguards, food allergen labelling, and family-friendly facilities everywhere Top Family Attractions 美ら海水族館 — Okinawa Churaumi Aquarium ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Location: Ocean Expo Park, Motobu Town

item.title: Okinawa Girls' Trip Guide: Resorts, Spa, Ryukyuan Culture & Beach Bliss
item.description: Okinawa is one of Japan’s most popular girls' trip destinations for good reason: the combination of beach resort luxury, excellent food, unique Ryukyuan craft culture, and the relaxed subtropical pace creates an atmosphere perfectly suited to groups of friends. Whether you want spa days by the ocean, cultural workshops, island-hopping, or simply great food and cocktails with ocean views, Okinawa delivers. Best Bases for a Girls' Trip Onna Village Resort Strip — Maximum Beach Luxury The main island’s resort coast offers the best facilities for groups: multiple restaurants, spa access, beach water sports, and nightlife within driving distance of Naha.
